title: Shi-part minimum representatives form a Garside shadow in finitely generated Coxeter groups
difficulty: The author replaces local maxima of Shi-component paths inside finite dihedral residues, proves termination by a lexicographic length-complexity measure, and establishes monotonicity of the minimum map by bipodal wall separation. These new geometric steps prove join and suffix closure of the full minimum set, beyond a Garside definition check.
scope: The selected problem is original Theorem1.2, that Shi-part minimum representatives form a Garside shadow for a Coxeter group with a finite generating set. Complete source Sections1--2 retain all wall/weak-order/Shi definitions, authored minimum existence via finite-dihedral residue path modification and descending lexicographic complexity, the full bipodal-wall monotonicity argument, join closure, suffix proof and terminal simple-generator inclusion. The named bipodality theorem and standard Coxeter residue projection facts remain their explicit original references. The independent cone-type-part results are unselected; their introductory statements and original printed noncore locators are supporting context only. The original bipodal wall picture remains fully editable native TikZ; no diagram/proof is invented and no mathematical text is repaired.
